top_concerns: Theory covers only single-worker eviction (largely classical paging/marking analysis); LBGR routing has no guarantee, so the 'unified' claim is overstated
Huge median latency/TTFT gains (11.8x/23x) with modest hit-rate and small P95 gains suggest the baseline is overloaded; no unsaturated-load comparison or variance reporting
Narrow baselines: only SGLang cache-aware/LRU, no other routers or eviction policies (LFU/ARC), no Belady oracle, unclear tuning of thresholds
LBGR lacks ablations (residual regression vs service-time+decay only, hyperparameter and calibration sensitivity, radix-tree estimate staleness)
Worst-case LRU competitive ratio and handcrafted round-robin order may not reflect real traces; short outputs, homogeneous workers, no production traces
